1251: Limitations
1252: The create_chart_from_prompt tool has the following limitations:
1253: Only sheet data sources are supported; reports and dashboards cannot be used as data sources.
1254: Complex multi-axis charts may require follow-up refinement via the refine_chart tool.
1255: Chart data is not rendered automatically — rendering must be handled separately as an artifact or inline visualization.
1256: When continuing a conversation, previous_message_id is required alongside conversation_id; omitting it prevents continuation.
1257: Use Cases
1258: The following items describe use cases for the create_chart_from_prompt tool:
1259: Quick data visualization: Rapidly generate a bar, line, or pie chart from sheet data using a simple plain-language request, without needing to configure chart parameters manually.
1260: Iterative chart refinement: Start a chart conversation, review the result, then continue the same conversation with a follow-up prompt to adjust grouping, filters, or chart type.
1261: Multi-metric dashboards: Generate several related charts or metrics in a single call and then add selected results to a dashboard using the add_charts_to_dashboard tool.
1262: Exploratory data analysis: Use alongside the get_chart_suggestions tool to discover meaningful visualizations for a sheet before committing to a specific chart type.
1263: Explainable reporting: Pair with the explain_chart tool to produce a plain-language summary of how a generated chart or metric was derived from the underlying data.
1264: create_chart_from_data
1265: Access scopes: none
1266: Builds a chart structure from pre-computed data values — supporting bar, line, pie, and stacked bar chart types. Unlike the create_chart_from_prompt tool, create_chart_from_data does not query any sheet; you supply the data values directly. The resulting chart definition must be rendered manually as an artifact or inline visualization.
1267: Best Practices
1268: The following items are best practices for using the create_chart_from_data tool:
1269: Use the create_chart_from_prompt tool instead when working from raw Smartsheet data, as it handles data extraction automatically.
1270: Pre-compute or extract all data values before calling this tool, since it does not perform any sheet queries.
1271: Match the number of entries in each dataset's data array to the number of entries in labels to ensure a well-formed chart.
1272: After the tool returns, always render the chart yourself using the labels from result.labelInfo.labels and the datasets from result.dataSetInfo.dataSets.
1273: Basic Parameters
1274: The create_chart_from_data tool has the following parameters:
1275: chart_type: The type of chart to render. Accepted values are bar, line, pie, and stacked_bar.
1276: datasets: An array of dataset objects. Each object has a data property (an array of numbers) and an optional label property for the series name.
1277: labels: Category labels used on the x-axis for bar and line charts, or as segment labels for pie charts.
1278: title: The chart title.
1279: data_format: How to format data values displayed in the chart. Accepted values are number, currency, and percent. The data_format parameter defaults to number.
1280: Key Features
1281: The create_chart_from_data tool has the following key features:
1282: Pre-computed data input: Accepts data you have already computed or extracted, giving you full control over what is charted without relying on a sheet query.
1283: Multiple chart types: Supports bar, line, pie, and stacked_bar chart types to cover a range of visualization needs.
1284: Multi-series support: Accepts multiple dataset objects in a single call, enabling side-by-side or layered series on the same chart.
1285: Flexible data formatting: Formats displayed values as plain numbers, currency, or percentages via the data_format parameter.
1286: Structured chart definition output: Returns a JSON chart definition containing labels and datasets that you use to render the chart as an artifact or inline visualization.
1287: Limitations
1288: The create_chart_from_data tool has the following limitations:
1289: Does not query any Smartsheet sheet data; all values must be provided by the caller.
1290: Cannot be refined using the refine_chart tool, as there is no backing conversation.
1291: Cannot be added to a dashboard via the add_charts_to_dashboard tool, since it has no conversation backing.
1292: Only supports the four chart types explicitly listed (bar, line, pie, stacked_bar); other chart types are not available.
1293: Does not validate that dataset lengths match the number of labels, so mismatches must be avoided by the caller.
1294: Use Cases
1295: The following items describe use cases for the create_chart_from_data tool:
1296: Visualizing externally sourced data: Charting data that originates outside Smartsheet, such as values from a CSV export, a database query, or a manual calculation.
1297: Displaying aggregated metrics: Rendering summary statistics or KPIs that have already been computed, without needing to re-query a sheet.
1298: Multi-series comparisons: Presenting multiple data series side by side — for example, comparing actual versus budgeted figures across several months.
1299: Percentage and currency breakdowns: Displaying financial distributions or completion rates using the currency or percent data formats for cleaner presentation.
1300: Custom chart construction: Building a precisely defined chart when the automatic AI-driven interpretation of the create_chart_from_prompt tool would not produce the exact structure needed.
1301: refine_chart
1302: Access scopes: READ_SHEETS
1303: The refine_chart tool retrieves suggested follow-up refinements for an existing chart within an active conversation. It does not itself modify or update the chart — it returns a list of suggested next steps that can be applied by making a subsequent call to the create_chart_from_prompt tool.
1304: Best Practices
1305: The following items are best practices for using the refine_chart tool:
1306: Use the create_chart_from_prompt tool before calling refine_chart to establish a valid conversation and obtain the required conversation_id and message_id.
1307: To apply a chosen refinement, call the create_chart_from_prompt tool with the same conversation_id, the previous_message_id, and the refinement's prompt.
1308: Basic Parameters
1309: The refine_chart tool has the following parameters:
1310: conversation_id — The conversation ID returned from the create_chart_from_prompt tool. This is required.
1311: message_id — The message ID of the chart or metric answer to refine. This is required, and the message must be an answer (chart or metric), not a question.
1312: count — The number of refinement suggestions to return. The count parameter defaults to 5, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 10.
1313: Key Features
1314: The refine_chart tool has the following key features:
1315: Suggestion-based refinement — Returns a set of suggested refinements, each with a title, prompt, chart type, and type, giving users structured options for improving their chart.
1316: Conversation continuity — Operates within an existing conversation started by the create_chart_from_prompt tool, preserving context across chart iterations.
1317: Configurable suggestion count — Allows the caller to control how many refinement suggestions are returned, up to a maximum of 10.
1318: Non-destructive operation — Does not alter the existing chart in any way; changes are only applied when a refinement prompt is passed to the create_chart_from_prompt tool.
1319: Limitations
1320: The refine_chart tool has the following limitations:
1321: Requires an active conversation established by the create_chart_from_prompt tool; it cannot be used independently or with charts created via the create_chart_from_data tool.
1322: Returns suggestions only — applying a refinement requires a separate follow-up call to the create_chart_from_prompt tool.
1323: The message_id must reference an answer message (a chart or metric); question messages are not valid targets.
1324: Charts created via create_chart_from_data cannot be refined using this tool, as they have no backing conversation.
1325: Use Cases
1326: The following items describe use cases for the refine_chart tool:
1327: Iterative chart improvement — After generating an initial chart with the create_chart_from_prompt tool, use refine_chart to surface actionable next steps for improving the visualization.
1328: Guided user experience — Present refinement suggestions to a user so they can select a direction for updating their chart without needing to write a new prompt from scratch.
1329: Chart type exploration — Use returned chartType values in suggestions to help users discover alternative chart types that may better represent their data.
1330: Multi-chart conversation management — In conversations that produce multiple charts or metrics, use refine_chart with a specific message_id to target refinements at a particular chart.
1331: explain_chart
1332: Access scopes: READ_SHEETS
1333: The explain_chart tool provides a plain-language explanation of how a chart or metric answer was produced within a charting conversation. It returns a summary and step-by-step reasoning describing the logic behind the chart, without modifying the chart itself.
1334: Best Practices
1335: The following items are best practices for using the explain_chart tool:
1336: Use explain_chart after generating a chart with the create_chart_from_prompt tool, to give stakeholders or reviewers a clear understanding of how the result was derived.
1337: When working with a chart that has been saved to a dashboard, supply the optional chart_id and chart_version parameters for the most accurate explanation.
1338: Confirm that the target message is an answer message (containing a chart or metric), not a question or prompt message, before calling the tool.
1339: Basic Parameters
1340: The explain_chart tool has the following parameters:
1341: conversation_id: The conversation ID from the create_chart_from_prompt tool. This parameter is required and identifies the active charting conversation containing the answer to explain.
1342: message_id: The message ID of the chart or metric answer to explain. This parameter is required and must reference an answer message, not a question.
1343: chart_id: An optional chart ID for a chart that has already been saved to a dashboard.
1344: chart_version: An optional chart version for a chart that has already been saved to a dashboard.
1345: Key Features
1346: The explain_chart tool has the following key features:
1347: Plain-language summary: Returns a human-readable summary describing how the chart or metric result was produced, making it easy to communicate methodology to non-technical stakeholders.
1348: Step-by-step reasoning: Breaks down the logic behind the chart into discrete steps, providing transparency into how the data was interpreted and visualized.
1349: Dashboard chart support: Accepts optional chart_id and chart_version parameters to explain charts that have been saved to a dashboard via the add_charts_to_dashboard tool.
1350: Conversation-scoped context: Operates within the context of an existing conversation started by the create_chart_from_prompt tool, meaning all relevant data and prompt history inform the explanation.
1351: Limitations
1352: The explain_chart tool has the following limitations:
1353: Requires an active conversation originally created by the create_chart_from_prompt tool — it cannot explain charts created through the create_chart_from_data tool, as those have no conversation backing.
1354: The message_id must reference an answer message (a chart or metric result), not a question or prompt message.
1355: Does not return updated chart data or a new visualization — it returns explanation text only.
1356: Cannot be used to modify, regenerate, or refine a chart; use the refine_chart tool for those operations.
1357: Use Cases
1358: The following items describe use cases for the explain_chart tool:
1359: Stakeholder transparency: Explain to a non-technical audience how a revenue or status chart was derived from sheet data, so they can trust and act on the results.
1360: Audit and review: Document the reasoning behind a dashboard chart during a project review or compliance audit, using the step-by-step explanation as a reference artifact.
1361: Debugging unexpected results: Investigate why a chart looks different than expected by reviewing the reasoning steps to spot incorrect column mappings or data interpretations.
1362: Onboarding and knowledge transfer: Help new team members understand what a saved dashboard chart represents and how it was built, without needing to recreate it.
1363: Multi-chart disambiguation: After the create_chart_from_prompt tool returns multiple chart messages in a single response, use explain_chart on a specific message ID to clarify what each individual chart represents before deciding which to refine or save.
1364: query_chart
1365: Access scopes: READ_SHEETS
1366: The query_chart tool queries a saved chart definition's data for visualization, returning the chart definition, data points, and styling needed for rendering. This tool is exclusively for charts that have already been saved to a dashboard via the add_charts_to_dashboard tool.
1367: Best Practices
1368: The following items are best practices for using the query_chart tool:
1369: Use the chart_id and version values returned directly from the add_charts_to_dashboard tool response, as these are the only reliable sources for those values.
1370: Do not call the get_dashboard tool to retrieve the chart_id or version, as chart widgets do not expose these fields through the public dashboard API.
1371: Do not use this tool after calling create_chart_from_prompt, as that tool returns chart data inline and does not produce a saved chart ID.
1372: Basic Parameters
1373: The query_chart tool has the following parameters:
1374: chart_id: A string representing the chart ID obtained from the add_charts_to_dashboard tool. This is a required parameter.
1375: version: A string representing the chart version obtained from the add_charts_to_dashboard tool. This is a required parameter.
1376: Key Features
1377: The query_chart tool has the following key features:
1378: Saved chart retrieval: Retrieves the full chart definition, including data points and styling, for a chart that has been saved to a Smartsheet dashboard.
1379: Visualization-ready output: Returns all data necessary to render the chart, including chart structure and configuration.
1380: Dashboard chart support: Works specifically within the context of charts added to dashboards, maintaining dashboard-specific context and styling.
1381: Limitations
1382: The query_chart tool has the following limitations:
1383: Requires a chart_id and version sourced exclusively from the add_charts_to_dashboard tool response.
1384: Does not work with conversation message IDs produced by the create_chart_from_prompt tool.
1385: The chart_id and version cannot be retrieved via the get_dashboard tool.
1386: Only applies to charts already saved to a dashboard; it cannot query unsaved or in-progress charts.
1387: Use Cases
1388: The following items describe use cases for the query_chart tool:
1389: Re-rendering a dashboard chart: Retrieves the data and styling for a previously saved chart so it can be rendered again in a visualization artifact or inline display.
1390: Inspecting saved chart data: Allows review of the underlying data points of a chart that was saved to a dashboard.
1391: Syncing chart state: Fetches the current definition of a saved chart to ensure the rendered visualization reflects the most up-to-date saved state on the dashboard.
1392: get_chart_definition
1393: Access scopes: READ_SHEETS
1394: Retrieves a saved chart definition — including its type, axes, styling, and configuration — for a chart that has already been saved to a dashboard via the add_charts_to_dashboard tool.
1395: Best Practices
1396: The following items are best practices for using the get_chart_definition tool:
1397: Use the chart_id and version values returned directly by the add_charts_to_dashboard tool, as these are the only reliable sources for these required values.
1398: Do not call the get_dashboard tool to retrieve chart_id or version, as chart widgets do not expose these fields through the public dashboard API.
1399: Do not call this tool after create_chart_from_prompt, as that tool returns chart data inline and no saved chart definition exists until the chart is added to a dashboard.
1400: Pass dashboard_id and widget_id when dashboard-specific styling needs to be reflected in the retrieved definition.
1401: Basic Parameters
1402: The get_chart_definition tool has the following parameters:
1403: chart_id: The chart ID from the add_charts_to_dashboard tool. This is a required string parameter.
1404: version: The chart version, also returned by the add_charts_to_dashboard tool. This is a required string parameter.
1405: dashboard_id: The dashboard ID, used to apply dashboard-specific styling. The dashboard_id parameter defaults to null.
1406: widget_id: The widget ID, used when the chart is placed on a dashboard. The widget_id parameter defaults to null.
1407: Key Features
1408: The get_chart_definition tool has the following key features:
1409: Chart type and configuration retrieval: Returns the complete chart definition, including chart type, axes configuration, and styling details.
1410: Dashboard-specific styling: Accepts optional dashboard_id and widget_id parameters to return styling that reflects the chart's appearance within a specific dashboard context.
1411: Version-aware retrieval: Uses a version string alongside the chart ID to ensure the desired iteration of a chart definition is retrieved.
1412: Limitations
1413: The get_chart_definition tool has the following limitations:
1414: Requires a chart_id and version obtained specifically from the add_charts_to_dashboard tool response; these values cannot be retrieved via the get_dashboard tool.
1415: Only works with charts that have been saved to a dashboard; it does not work with conversation message IDs or charts created inline via create_chart_from_prompt that have not yet been added to a dashboard.
1416: Use Cases
1417: The following items describe use cases for the get_chart_definition tool:
1418: Inspecting a saved chart: Retrieve the full configuration of a chart that was previously saved to a dashboard to review its type, axes, and styling settings.
1419: Debugging chart appearance: Examine the chart definition alongside dashboard and widget context to understand why a chart renders in a particular way.
1420: Auditing dashboard charts: Review chart definitions as part of a broader audit of dashboard content and visualization standards.
1421: Pre-refinement review: Inspect an existing chart definition before initiating a refinement workflow to understand what changes are needed.
1422: add_charts_to_dashboard
1423: Access scopes: CREATE_SIGHTS
1424: The add_charts_to_dashboard tool adds one or more previously created charts to a Smartsheet dashboard as new widgets in a single request. Each chart must have been created via the create_chart_from_prompt tool or refined via the refine_chart tool before it can be added. The tool returns a dashboardPermalink that links directly to the dashboard, and one result per chart, in the order the charts were supplied.
1425: This tool is unavailable for the Microsoft 365 Copilot Connector (the Copilot Studio connector for Copilot Chat)
1426: Best Practices
1427: The following items are best practices for using the add_charts_to_dashboard tool:
1428: Pass every chart destined for the same dashboard in one call, even when there is only one chart.
1429: Don't add charts to the same dashboard with several calls in parallel. Each call places its widgets independently, so parallel calls can leave widgets overlapping.
1430: For more than 10 charts, make consecutive calls and wait for each call to finish before starting the next one.
1431: Verify that the target dashboard ID is correct before calling this tool, using the list_dashboards tool or the get_dashboard tool if needed.
1432: Check each entry in results. A successful call doesn't mean every chart was added, so tell the user which charts were added and which weren't.
1433: Only retry entries whose reason is NOT_ATTEMPTED, because those charts were never sent. Any other reason may already have created the widget, so retrying risks a duplicate.
1434: Surface the returned dashboardPermalink to the user as a "View on dashboard" link so they can immediately see the result.
1435: Basic Parameters
1436: The add_charts_to_dashboard tool has the following parameters:
1437: dashboard_id — An integer representing the ID of the dashboard where the chart widgets are placed.
1438: charts — An array of 1 to 10 charts to add, in the order they should appear. Each chart has the following properties:
1439: conversationId — A string representing the conversation ID returned from the chart creation or refinement response.
1440: messageId — A string representing the message ID of the specific chart response to add.
1441: messageType — A string representing the message type from the chart creation or refinement response (messages[].messageType). The value must be v2/ChartMessage.
1442: Key Features
1443: The add_charts_to_dashboard tool has the following key features:
1444: Multiple charts in one call — Adds up to 10 charts to a dashboard in one request, placing them one after another so they don't overlap.
1445: Per-chart results — Returns one entry per chart, in request order. Each entry has a type of SUCCEEDED or FAILED. A failed entry includes a reason, such as NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED, or NOT_ATTEMPTED.
1446: Conversation-based workflow — Ties directly into the conversation flow started by the create_chart_from_prompt tool, using the conversationId and messageId from that flow to identify exactly which result to publish.
1447: Dashboard permalink — Returns a dashboardPermalink, giving immediate access to the live dashboard view.
1448: Widget metadata — Returns a chartId, version, and widgetId for each added chart that can be used with the get_chart_definition tool and the query_chart tool for further inspection or rendering.
1449: Non-destructive placement — Adds each chart as a new widget without moving or altering any existing widgets on the dashboard.
1450: Limitations
1451: The add_charts_to_dashboard tool has the following limitations:
1452: The user must have edit access to the target dashboard; the tool does not succeed with view-only permissions.
1453: Only charts created through the conversation flow (via the create_chart_from_prompt tool or the refine_chart tool) can be added; manually defined charts are not supported.
1454: Metrics can't be added to a dashboard. If any chart's messageType isn't v2/ChartMessage, the call is rejected and no charts are added.
1455: All charts in a call go to one dashboard; use one call per dashboard.
1456: Each chart is added as a new widget; the tool does not update or replace an existing widget.
1457: If a chart fails, charts already added by the same call stay on the dashboard.
1458: Use Cases
1459: The following items describe use cases for the add_charts_to_dashboard tool:
1460: Publishing an AI-generated chart — After using the create_chart_from_prompt tool to generate a chart from sheet data, use this tool to publish that chart directly onto an operational or executive dashboard.
1461: Multi-chart deployment — When a create_chart_from_prompt response returns several charts, add the ones you want to a dashboard in a single call.
1462: Iterative dashboard building — Combine with the refine_chart tool to iteratively improve a chart before finalizing and publishing it to a dashboard.
1463: Sharing
1464: This section describes Smartsheet MCP server tools for sharing assets with groups and other users.
1465: list_shares
1466: Access scopes: ADMIN_WORKSPACES, SHARE_SHEETS, SHARE_SIGHTS
1467: Toolset: sharing
1468: The list_shares tool retrieves a list of all users and groups with whom a Smartsheet asset has been shared. It returns share details including access levels, user and group information, and share scope, making it useful for understanding who has access to a given asset.
1469: Best Practices
1470: The following items are best practices for using the list_shares tool:
1471: Use the sharing_include parameter to narrow results when you only need direct shares versus inherited workspace shares, as this reduces noise in the response.
1472: When auditing permissions across assets with many collaborators, paginate through all results using last_key before drawing conclusions, since each page returns up to 100 shares.
1473: Combine results from the list_shares tool with the the list_sheets or the browse_workspace tool to build a comprehensive access map across multiple assets.
1474: Basic Parameters
1475: The list_shares tool has the following parameters:
1476: asset_id: The integer ID of the asset whose shares are being listed. This is a required parameter.
1477: asset_type: The type of asset being queried. Accepted values are sheet, report, sight, workspace, collection, and file. This is a required parameter.
1478: last_key: A pagination token used to retrieve the next page of results when an asset has more than 100 shares. Omit the last_key parameter to get the first page of results.
1479: sharing_include: An optional filter for share scope. Use ITEM to return only direct shares, or WORKSPACE to include shares inherited from a parent workspace. The sharing_include parameter defaults to null, meaning no scope filter is applied.
1480: Key Features
1481: The list_shares tool has the following key features:
1482: Multi-asset type support: Works across sheets, reports, sights (dashboards), workspaces, collections, and files, providing a unified way to audit sharing across different Smartsheet content types.
1483: Share scope filtering: The sharing_include parameter lets callers distinguish between shares applied directly to an item (ITEM) and those inherited from a workspace (WORKSPACE).
1484: Access level detail: Each returned share includes the collaborator's access level (e.g., viewer, editor, admin), enabling permission auditing without navigating the Smartsheet UI.
1485: Limitations
1486: The list_shares tool has the following limitations:
1487: Only assets the calling user has permission to view are accessible; shares on assets outside the user's access cannot be retrieved.
1488: Each page returns a maximum of 100 shares, requiring multiple calls with pagination for heavily shared assets.
1489: Use Cases
1490: The following items describe use cases for the list_shares tool:
1491: Permission auditing: Review all users and groups who have access to a specific sheet or workspace to ensure the right people have the right access levels.
1492: Offboarding checks: Verify whether a departing team member still has access to sensitive Smartsheet assets before revoking their access.
1493: Compliance reporting: Generate an access report for a workspace or collection to satisfy internal governance or external compliance requirements.
1494: Access comparison: Compare share lists across multiple assets to identify inconsistencies, such as a report being shared more broadly than its underlying sheet.
1495: Inherited vs. direct share investigation: Use the sharing_include filter to determine whether a user's access to an item is directly granted or inherited from a parent workspace.
1496: Favorites
1497: The following sections describe Smartsheet MCP server tools for marking assets as favorites and operating on your list of favorites.
1498: list_favorites
1499: Access scopes: READ_SHEETS
1500: Toolset: sharing
1501: The list_favorites tool retrieves a list of all items marked as favorites by the current user. Favorites can include sheets, reports, dashboards (sights), folders, workspaces, and templates, making it a quick way to discover and access frequently used resources.
1502: Best Practices
1503: The following items describe best practices for using the list_favorites tool:
1504: Iterate through pages when the user has a large number of favorites, since pagination is always enforced.
1505: Use page_size to balance response size and performance based on your use case.
1506: Basic Parameters
1507: The list_favorites tool has the following parameters:
1508: page (optional) — The number of the page to retrieve, starting at 1. The page number defaults to 1.
1509: page_size (optional) — The number of items per page, between 1 and 100. The page_size defaults to 100.
1510: Key Features
1511: The list_favorites tool has the following key features:
1512: Multi-type support — Returns favorites across all supported asset types: sheets, reports, dashboards (sights), folders, workspaces, and templates.
1513: Paginated results — Pagination is always enforced, allowing controlled retrieval of large favorites lists.
1514: Quick resource discovery — Serves as a fast index for locating frequently accessed Smartsheet resources without searching the broader account.
1515: Limitations
1516: The maximum page size is 100 items per page.
1517: Use Cases
1518: The following items describe use cases for the list_favorites tool:
1519: Dashboard building — Retrieve a user's favorites to populate a personalized home screen or quick-access panel.
1520: Audit and inventory — List all favorited assets to understand which resources a user relies on most frequently.
1521: Navigation shortcuts — Fetch favorites at session start to build a shortcut menu for rapid navigation to key sheets and reports.
1522: is_favorite
1523: Access scopes: READ_SHEETS
1524: Toolset: sharing
1525: The is_favorite tool checks if a specific asset is marked as a favorite by the current user. Use this tool to determine the favorite status of a sheet, report, dashboard, folder, workspace, or template.
1526: Best Practices
1527: The following items describe best practices for using the is_favorite tool:
1528: Use the include parameter with "name" to enrich responses with human-readable context when displaying results to users.
1529: Handle 404 responses gracefully, as a 404 indicates the asset is simply not favorited rather than a system error.
1530: Basic Parameters
1531: The is_favorite tool has the following parameters:
1532: asset_id — The ID of the asset to check.
1533: asset_type — The type of asset to check. Valid values are workspace, folder, sheet, report, template, and sight (dashboard).
1534: include — A comma-separated list of optional elements to include in the response. Valid values are "directId" and "name". The include parameter defaults to null.
1535: Key Features
1536: The is_favorite tool has the following key features:
1537: Multi-asset type support — Supports all major Smartsheet asset types: workspaces, folders, sheets, reports, templates, and sights (dashboards).
1538: Optional enrichment — Accepts an include parameter to return additional details such as the asset's name or direct ID alongside the favorite status.
1539: Limitations
1540: The is_favorite tool returns a 404 Not Found error if the asset is not marked as a favorite by the user, rather than returning a false or empty result.
1541: Use Cases
1542: The following items describe use cases for the is_favorite tool:
1543: Conditional UI state — Determine whether to display a "Add to Favorites" or "Remove from Favorites" option in a custom interface.
1544: Audit and reporting — Verify the favorite status of specific assets as part of a broader user preference or workspace audit workflow.
1545: Workflow automation — Check favorite status as a conditional step in an automated workflow that behaves differently based on whether an asset is bookmarked.
1546: add_favorites
1547: Access scopes: ADMIN_WORKSPACES
1548: Toolset: sharing
1549: The add_favorites tool marks one or more Smartsheet assets as favorites for the current user, enabling quick access to frequently used resources. It supports bulk operations across a variety of asset types, including sheets, reports, dashboards, folders, workspaces, and templates.
1550: Best Practices
1551: A best practices for using the add_favorites tool is to batch multiple favorites into a single request (up to 100) rather than making repeated individual calls.
1552: Basic Parameters
1553: The add_favorites tool has the following parameters:
1554: favorites — A list of favorite objects to add, where each object contains an objectId (the asset's numeric ID) and a type (the kind of asset being favorited). At least one item is required, and up to 100 items may be submitted in a single request.
1555: Key Features
1556: The add_favorites tool has the following key features:
1557: Bulk operations — Up to 100 favorites can be added in a single request, reducing the number of API calls needed for large-scale operations.
1558: Multi-type support — Supports favoriting assets of different types in the same request, including workspaces, folders, sheets, reports, templates, and sights (dashboards).
1559: Idempotent behavior — Assets that are already favorited are silently ignored without returning an error, making repeated calls safe.
1560: Limitations
1561: The add_favorites tool has the following limitations:
1562: A maximum of 100 favorites can be added in a single request.
1563: Only private sheet-type template IDs are allowed when the type is template.
1564: Use Cases
1565: The following items describe use cases for the add_favorites tool:
1566: Onboarding setup — Quickly favorite a curated set of key sheets, dashboards, and workspaces for a new team member so they have immediate access to the most important resources.
1567: Project kickoff — At the start of a project, favorite all relevant sheets, reports, and folders so the project team can navigate to them without searching.

1574: The delete_favorites tool removes one or more items from the current user's list of favorites in Smartsheet. It supports bulk removal of sheets, reports, dashboards, folders, workspaces, or templates in a single operation. 1580: asset_type — The type of asset being unfavorited. Accepted values are workspace, folder, sheet, report, template, or sight.

1582: The delete_favorites tool has the following key features:
1583: Bulk removal — Up to 10 favorites of the same type can be removed in a single request, reducing the number of API calls needed for cleanup operations.

1586: The delete_favorites tool has the following limitations:

1733: create_project_template
1734: Access scopes: ADMIN_WORKSPACES
1735: Toolset: portfolio
1736: create_project_template creates a new project template within a portfolio. A project template copies the structure of a source workspace at creation time, and each project provisioned from it inherits the same sheets, dashboards, reports, and other items. The source workspace is not modified.
1737: Best Practices
1738: The following items are best practices for using the create_project_template tool:
1739: Omit asset_source unless the user explicitly provides a workspace ID or folder ID to use as the template source — do not infer or select a source workspace by default.
1740: Use the browse_workspace tool or the search tool to confirm a source workspace ID before passing it as asset_source.
1741: After creation, use the get_project_template tool to retrieve the workspaceId and customize the template workspace before provisioning projects from it.
1742: Basic Parameters
1743: The create_project_template tool has the following parameters:
1744: portfolio_id — The UUID of the portfolio in which to create the project template. This parameter is required.
1745: name — The name to assign to the new project template. Must be between 1 and 50 characters. This parameter is required.
1746: asset_source — An optional source asset whose structure is copied into the project template at creation time. When provided, requires:
1747: asset_type — The type of source asset: workspace or folder.
1748: asset_id — The integer ID of the source workspace or folder.
1749: The asset_source parameter defaults to null.
1750: Key Features
1751: The create_project_template tool has the following key features:
1752: Blank or source-based creation — Creates a project template from scratch when asset_source is omitted, or copies the structure of an existing workspace or folder when asset_source is provided.
1753: Non-destructive source handling — When a source workspace or folder is specified, its contents are copied at creation time and the original is not modified.
1754: Inherited project structure — Every project provisioned from the template inherits the same sheets, dashboards, reports, and other items present in the template workspace.
1755: Result message — Returns a message field (SUCCESS or PARTIAL_SUCCESS) and a resultCode (0 for success, 3 for partial success) alongside the created project template object.
1756: Limitations
1757: The create_project_template tool has the following limitations:
1758: Project template names must be between 1 and 50 characters.
1759: asset_source copies workspace structure only at creation time — subsequent changes to the source workspace are not reflected in the template.
1760: The template workspace workspaceId may be null immediately after creation until provisioning completes.
1761: Use Cases
1762: The following items describe use cases for the create_project_template tool:
1763: Blank template creation — Creates an empty project template workspace within a portfolio that can be customized by adding sheets, dashboards, and reports before any projects are provisioned from it.
1764: Template from existing workspace — Copies the structure of an existing workspace into a new project template so that its layout and asset organization become the standard for all future projects provisioned from it.
1765: Template from folder — Uses a specific folder's structure as the basis for a project template, enabling fine-grained control over which assets are included.
1766: Multi-template portfolios — Adds additional project templates to a portfolio to support different project types or workflows beyond the default "Standard template."

1918: Use last_key from each response to paginate through large result sets.

1924: max_items — Maximum number of items to return per page. Accepted range is 1–100. The max_items parameter defaults to 10.
1925: Key Features
1926: The get_scenario_groups tool has the following key features:
1927: Embedded child scenarios — When include_scenarios is true, each plan includes its child scenarios with fields such as taskId, name, provisioningStatus, isApplied, sourceSheetIds, and calculated metrics.
1928: Source sheet IDs — Each scenario plan and child scenario exposes sourceSheetIds, which can be used with other Smartsheet tools to inspect or update the underlying project sheets.
1929: Pagination support — Returns results in pages using a lastKey cursor, allowing efficient traversal of large result sets.
1930: Permission flags — Returns permissions on each plan (and each scenario when included) indicating whether the current user can view, edit, delete, share, or apply.
1931: Use Cases
1932: The following items describe use cases for the get_scenario_groups tool:
1933: Scenario plan discovery — List all scenario plans accessible in the organization or within a specific workspace before exploring individual scenarios.
1934: Scenario ID resolution — Set include_scenarios to true to retrieve child scenario taskId values needed as input for get_scenario_diffs or get_scenario_capacity_workload.
1935: Scenario status review — Inspect isApplied and provisioningStatus fields on child scenarios to understand which plan is currently active and which are alternatives.
1936: get_scenario_group
1937: Toolset: scenario_planning
1938: get_scenario_group returns a single scenario plan by ID from the Resource Management (RM) service. Use it when the scenario plan ID is already known to fetch the plan, its child scenarios, and optionally the latest metrics for a time window.
1939: Best Practices
1940: The following items are best practices for using the get_scenario_group tool:
1941: Prefer get_scenario_group over the get_scenario_groups tool when the scenario plan ID is already known.
1942: When fetching metrics for a scenario plan, pass start_date with end_date to scope them to a custom time window.
1943: Always supply start_date and end_date together when using a custom metrics window — neither is valid without the other.
1944: Basic Parameters
1945: The get_scenario_group tool has the following parameters:
1946: scenario_group_id (required) — ID of the scenario plan to retrieve. Must be greater than 0.
1947: include_scenarios — Whether to embed child scenarios in the response. The include_scenarios parameter defaults to true.
1948: start_date — Start of the custom metrics window (YYYY-MM-DD); requires end_date. The start_date parameter defaults to null.
1949: end_date — End of the custom metrics window (YYYY-MM-DD); requires start_date. The end_date parameter defaults to null.
1950: Key Features
1951: The get_scenario_group tool has the following key features:
1952: Child scenario embedding — When include_scenarios is true (the default), the response embeds all child scenarios with their full metadata, including status, permissions, and calculated metrics.
1953: Custom metrics window — Passing start_date and end_date scopes the returned metrics to a specific time period, enabling time-bounded capacity and project analysis.
1954: Rich scenario metrics — Each embedded scenario can include capacity data per user, discipline, and role; over/under-capacity summaries; tasks at risk; project stats; and windowed duration data.
1955: Baseline delta comparison — Non-baseline scenarios include a delta field comparing their metrics against the baseline (delay, duration, user count, and capacity changes).
1956: Permission flags — The response includes per-user permission flags (view, edit, delete, share, apply) for both the scenario plan and each child scenario.
1957: Limitations
1958: The get_scenario_group tool has the following limitations:
1959: When specifying a custom metrics window, both start_date and end_date must be provided together.
1960: Use Cases
1961: The following items describe use cases for the get_scenario_group tool:
1962: Fetching a known scenario plan — Retrieve the full details of a scenario plan when the ID is already available from a prior listing or creation call.
1963: Reviewing child scenarios — Inspect all child scenarios under a plan, including their status, applied/preferred flags, and associated Smartsheet sheet and folder IDs.
1964: Analyzing capacity over a date range — Pass start_date and end_date to retrieve metrics for a specific planning window, enabling capacity analysis for a sprint, quarter, or fiscal period.
1965: Comparing scenarios against the baseline — Read the delta fields on non-baseline scenarios to assess how duration, delay, user count, and capacity differ from the plan's baseline.
1966: Checking user permissions — Verify what actions the current user can perform on the scenario plan and its child scenarios (view, edit, delete, share, apply).
1967: create_scenario_group
1968: Toolset: scenario_planning
1969: create_scenario_group creates a new scenario plan in a Smartsheet workspace. A scenario plan is a named collection of scenarios that explore different resource allocation and scheduling options for a set of projects. Creating a scenario plan creates only a baseline scenario.
1970: Best Practices
1971: The following items are best practices for using the create_scenario_group tool:
1972: Call get_scenario_groups first to check whether a scenario plan with the same name already exists in the target workspace.
1973: Use the id field from browse_workspace results to obtain numeric sheet IDs for the source_sheet_ids parameter.
1974: Basic Parameters
1975: The create_scenario_group tool has the following parameters:
1976: workspace_id — The encoded or numeric ID of the workspace in which to create the scenario plan. This parameter is required.
1977: name — The display name for the new scenario plan. This parameter is required.
1978: source_sheet_ids — An array of 1–5 numeric Smartsheet sheet IDs to associate with the plan. This parameter is required.
1979: Key Features
1980: The create_scenario_group tool has the following key features:
1981: Automatic baseline creation — Automatically creates a baseline scenario as the first child of the new scenario plan; the returned result contains the created baseline scenario.
1982: Multi-sheet association — Supports associating 1–5 source sheets with a single scenario plan, enabling multi-project scenario planning.
1983: Permalink access — Returns a permalink in the result so users can navigate directly to the new scenario plan.
1984: Limitations
1985: The create_scenario_group tool has the following limitations:
1986: You must have at least Admin permissions on the workspace where you create the plan and an Admin on all project sheets that you include.
1987: The source sheets must all belong to the same Resource Management organization and have Workload Tracking enabled.
1988: A maximum of 5 source sheets may be associated with a single scenario plan.
1989: Requires an Enterprise plan with the Scenario Planning feature enabled.
1990: Use Cases
1991: The following items describe use cases for the create_scenario_group tool:
1992: New scenario plan setup — Create a named scenario plan in a workspace to begin exploring alternative resource and scheduling options for one or more projects.
1993: Multi-project planning — Associate up to 5 project sheets with a single scenario plan to model tradeoffs across an entire portfolio of work.
1994: delete_scenario_group
1995: Toolset: scenario_planning
1996: delete_scenario_group permanently deletes a scenario plan and all of its scenarios from a Smartsheet workspace. This operation cannot be undone. (⚠️ destructive, irreversible)
1997: Basic Parameters
1998: The delete_scenario_group tool has the following parameters:
1999: scenario_group_id — The numeric database ID of the scenario plan to delete. This parameter is required. Obtain it from get_scenario_groups.

2001: The delete_scenario_group tool has the following key features:
2002: Complete removal — Deletes the scenario group and all child scenarios, including the baseline scenario, in a single operation.
2003: Limitations
2004: The delete_scenario_group tool has the following limitations:

2006: All scenarios within the scenario plan — including the baseline — are deleted along with the scenario plan.
2007: Use Cases
2008: The following items describe use cases for the delete_scenario_group tool:
2009: Clean up completed planning cycles — Remove a scenario plan after a planning cycle is complete and all decisions have been finalized and applied to source sheets.
2010: Remove abandoned plans — Delete scenario plans that were created for exploration but are no longer relevant or needed by the team.
2011: create_scenario
2012: Toolset: scenario_planning
2013: create_scenario adds a new scenario to an existing scenario plan (also called a scenario plan). Use this tool after create_scenario_group has established a baseline scenario to add alternative "what-if" scenarios for comparison.
2014: Best Practices
2015: The following items are best practices for using the create_scenario tool:
2016: Use a descriptive name (such as "Optimistic" or "Headcount Freeze") that clearly identifies what the scenario represents.
2017: After the tool returns, check result.provisioningStatus: COMPLETED means the scenario is ready to use; IN_PROGRESS or UPDATING means it is still being set up — refresh the scenario plan page within a minute; FAILED means setup did not succeed.
2018: Basic Parameters
2019: The create_scenario tool has the following parameters:
2020: scenario_group_id — The numeric database ID of the scenario plan to add the scenario to. This parameter is required. Obtain it from get_scenario_groups.
2021: name — The display name for the new scenario. This parameter is required.
2022: Key Features
2023: The create_scenario tool has the following key features:
2024: Alternative scenario creation — Adds a named "what-if" scenario to an existing scenario plan so it can be compared against the baseline and other scenarios.
2025: Provisioning status — Returns a provisioningStatus field (COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, UPDATING, FAILED, or UNKNOWN) indicating whether the scenario setup is complete.
2026: Limitations
2027: The create_scenario tool has the following limitations:
2028: A scenario plan can contain a maximum of 4 scenarios total, including the baseline.
2029: Cannot create a scenario outside of an existing scenario plan. Use create_scenario_group to create a new scenario plan first.
2030: Use Cases
2031: The following items describe use cases for the create_scenario tool:
2032: What-if analysis — Create an alternative scenario (such as "Delayed Start" or "Reduced Headcount") within an existing scenario plan to model different resource allocation outcomes.
2033: Comparative planning — Add multiple named scenarios to a plan to compare project timelines, capacity utilization, and over/under-capacity indicators side by side before committing to a plan.
2034: Iterative exploration — Build up a scenario plan incrementally by adding scenarios one at a time, evaluating each with the get_scenario_diffs tool and the get_scenario_capacity_workload tool before adding the next.
2035: get_scenario_diffs
2036: Toolset: scenario_planning
2037: get_scenario_diffs computes and returns all cell, row, and column differences between a scenario and its source sheets, including blocking and non-blocking conflicts and an aggregate apply-eligibility summary. Use this tool before applying a scenario to explain exactly what would change and whether apply is blocked.
2038: Basic Parameters
2039: The get_scenario_diffs tool has the following parameters:
2040: scenario_id — The taskId of the scenario to compute diffs for. This parameter is required. Obtain it from get_scenario_groups with include_scenarios=true.
2041: Key Features
2042: The get_scenario_diffs tool has the following key features:
2043: Cell-level diffs — Returns every changed cell grouped by row, with scenario and source values, column titles, column types, and column tags.
2044: Row and column additions and deletions — Lists rows and columns that exist only in the scenario, only in the source, or that have been deleted from either side.
2045: Blocking and non-blocking conflicts — Identifies per-sheet conflicts (such as type changes, formula additions, or user-added rows) and flags whether each conflict prevents applying the scenario.
2046: Aggregate apply-eligibility summary — The top-level summary object reports total sheets, conflict counts, cell diff counts, and the can_apply_all_sheets boolean so you can determine apply eligibility at a glance.
2047: Per-sheet diff summaries — Each sheet diff includes a sheet_summary with counts for cell diffs, row and column additions, deletions, and conflicts without requiring traversal of every detail array.
2048: Limitations
2049: The get_scenario_diffs tool has the following limitations:
2050: You must have at least Editor permissions on the workspace and all of the project sheets.
2051: Use Cases
2052: The following items describe use cases for the get_scenario_diffs tool:
2053: Pre-apply review — Inspect all changes a scenario would make to source sheets before committing, so stakeholders can confirm the impact.
2054: Conflict resolution — Surface blocking conflicts and their types to understand what must be resolved before a scenario can be applied.
2055: Change summary reporting — Use summary and per-sheet sheet_summary counts to produce a concise change report across all affected sheets.
2056: Assignee comparison — Compare totalSourceAssignees and totalScenarioAssignees to understand how resource assignments shift between the current plan and the scenario.
2057: get_scenario_capacity_workload
2058: Toolset: scenario_planning
2059: get_scenario_capacity_workload returns capacity (available hours) and workload (assigned hours) for a scenario over a specified date range, broken down by time bucket and grouped by user, discipline, or role. Use it to assess whether a scenario creates over- or under-capacity situations before applying it.
2060: Best Practices
2061: The following items are best practices for using the get_scenario_capacity_workload tool:
2062: Use group_names (preferred over group_ids) to filter results to specific people, disciplines, or roles.
2063: Compute utilization as workload_hours / total_hours; note that placeholder users do not have capacities.
2064: Use instant_type=month for broad planning views (up to a 6-month range) and instant_type=week for detailed scheduling views (up to 26 weeks).
2065: Basic Parameters
2066: The get_scenario_capacity_workload tool has the following parameters:
2067: scenario_id — The taskId of the scenario to query. This parameter is required. Obtain it from get_scenario_groups with include_scenarios=true.
2068: start_date — Start of the date range, inclusive, in YYYY-MM-DD format. This parameter is required.
2069: end_date — End of the date range, inclusive, in YYYY-MM-DD format. This parameter is required.
2070: group_type — Grouping dimension for the results. Accepted values are USER, DISCIPLINE, and RESOURCE_TYPE. The group_type parameter defaults to USER.
2071: instant_type — Time bucket size for the columns. Accepted values are month and week. The instant_type parameter defaults to month.
2072: group_names — Optional list of group display names to filter results. Groups not in this list still appear in the response with 0 hours.
2073: group_ids — Optional list of RM-native group IDs (rmUserId or rmTagId) to filter results. Use group_names instead when display names are available.
2074: filter_roles — Optional list of role names. Only assignments matching these roles contribute non-zero hours.
2075: filter_disciplines — Optional list of discipline names. Only assignments matching these disciplines contribute non-zero hours.
2076: filter_locations — Optional list of location names. Only assignments matching these locations contribute non-zero hours.
2077: filter_assignment_status — Optional assignment-status filter. Accepted values are confirmed for licensed users or placeholder for placeholder resources. For example, confirmed filters on only licensed user capacity and placeholder filters on only placeholder workload hours. Groups with non-matching assignments return 0 hours.
2078: Key Features
2079: The get_scenario_capacity_workload tool has the following key features:
2080: Capacity vs. workload matrix — Returns available total hours and assigned workload hours for each group, keyed by group display name and time bucket label, making it straightforward to calculate utilization.
2081: Flexible grouping — Supports grouping by individual users (USER), discipline (DISCIPLINE), or role (RESOURCE_TYPE) to match different planning perspectives.
2082: Weekly or monthly bucketing — Allows switching between weekly and monthly time buckets to adjust the level of scheduling granularity.
2083: Targeted filtering — Accepts filters by group name, role, discipline, location, and assignment status so that queries can be scoped to exactly the population you care about.
2084: Limitations
2085: The get_scenario_capacity_workload tool has the following limitations:
2086: You must have at least Editor permissions on the workspace and all of the project sheets.
2087: instant_type=month allows at most a 6-month date range; instant_type=week allows at most 26 weeks.
2088: Placeholder users do not have capacity values; only workload hours are returned for them.
2089: Date-range and filter values are validated by the service and may return descriptive errors if invalid.
2090: Use Cases
2091: The following items describe use cases for the get_scenario_capacity_workload tool:
2092: Over-capacity identification — Compare workload hours against available hours per user, discipline or role to find bottlenecks before a scenario is applied.
2093: Resource utilization analysis — Calculate utilization ratios for each team member, discipline or role over a planning horizon to guide staffing decisions.
2094: Scenario comparison — Run this tool against multiple scenarios to compare capacity impact side by side before committing to one.
2095: Filtered team view — Pass group_names, filter_disciplines, or filter_roles to focus the response on a specific team or skill set, reducing noise from unrelated resource groups.
2096: Placeholder vs. confirmed workload — Use filter_assignment_status to separate confirmed assignments from placeholder allocations for more accurate capacity planning.
2097: apply_scenario
2098: Toolset: scenario_planning
2099: apply_scenario applies a scenario's diffs to its source sheets. The operation is accepted asynchronously — a successful response means the apply request was accepted, not that the source sheets have finished updating. (⚠️ destructive)
2100: Best Practices
2101: The following items are best practices for using the apply_scenario tool:
2102: Call get_scenario_diffs first to check for blocking conflicts before calling this tool. The tool returns an error if any source sheet has blocking conflicts.
2103: Basic Parameters
2104: The apply_scenario tool has the following parameters:
2105: scenario_id — The taskId of the scenario whose diffs should be applied to source sheets. This parameter is required. Obtain it from get_scenario_groups with include_scenarios=true.
2106: Key Features
2107: The apply_scenario tool has the following key features:
2108: Asynchronous application — Accepts the apply request immediately and returns a success response while source sheet updates continue in the background.
2109: Diff-based updates — Writes only the changes captured in the scenario's diffs back to the source sheets, leaving unchanged data intact.
2110: Limitations
2111: The apply_scenario tool has the following limitations:
2112: You must have at least Admin permissions on the workspace and all of the project sheets.
2113: Returns an error if the scenario plan already has an applied scenario, or if any source sheet has blocking conflicts. Call get_scenario_diffs first to check for blocking conflicts before calling this tool.
2114: Baseline scenarios cannot be applied; only non-baseline scenarios are eligible.
2115: Requires apply permission on the scenario plan, editor access on all source sheets, and an Enterprise plan with the Scenario Planning feature enabled.
2116: Use Cases
2117: The following items describe use cases for the apply_scenario tool:
2118: Commit a chosen plan — After reviewing scenario diffs and confirming no blocking conflicts exist, apply the preferred scenario to make its changes live across all source sheets.
2119: Finalize resource allocation — Apply a scenario that resolves over-capacity issues or optimizes project timelines once stakeholders have reviewed and approved the plan.
2120: get_shadow_sheet
2121: Toolset: scenario_planning
2122: get_shadow_sheet retrieves a scenario sheet — a scenario-specific copy of a source sheet used by Scenario Planning. The tool returns the sheet structure including columns and rows.
2123: Best Practices
2124: The following items are best practices for using the get_shadow_sheet tool:
2125: Call the get_scenario_groups tool with include_scenarios=true first to obtain the scenario sheet ID from the source_sheet_ids field of a scenario.
2126: Use the exclude parameter to omit cell fields you don't need — such as value and displayValue — to reduce payload size when only column metadata is required.
2127: Call this tool before using the add_shadow_sheet_rows tool, the update_shadow_sheet_rows tool, or the delete_shadow_sheet_rows tool to confirm column IDs and existing row IDs.
2128: Basic Parameters
2129: The get_shadow_sheet tool has the following parameters:
2130: sheet_id — The ID of the scenario sheet to retrieve. This parameter is required. Obtain it from the source_sheet_ids field of a scenario returned by the get_scenario_groups tool with include_scenarios=true.
2131: exclude — An optional list of elements to omit from the response. Accepted values are filteredOutRows, linkInFromCellDetails, linksOutToCellsDetails, nonexistentCells, cellLinks, value, displayValue, image, and imageAltText. The exclude parameter defaults to null.
2132: page — The page number for paginating rows (1-based). The page parameter defaults to 1.
2133: page_size — The number of rows per page. Maximum 500. The page_size parameter defaults to 100.
2134: Key Features
2135: The get_shadow_sheet tool has the following key features:
2136: Full sheet structure — Returns the scenario sheet's columns and rows, providing the complete structure needed to inspect or modify scenario data.
2137: Payload reduction — The exclude parameter omits specific cell fields to reduce response size when only partial cell data is needed.
2138: Limitations
2139: The get_shadow_sheet tool has the following limitations:
2140: The caller must have at least Editor permissions on the workspace and all associated project sheets.
2141: The results don't include a permalink or workspace for the sheet, because the sheets are inaccessible.
2142: Use Cases
2143: The following items describe use cases for the get_shadow_sheet tool:
2144: Pre-edit inspection — Retrieve a scenario sheet's column IDs and existing row IDs before calling the add_shadow_sheet_rows tool, the update_shadow_sheet_rows tool, or the delete_shadow_sheet_rows tool.
2145: Scenario state review — Inspect the current data in a scenario sheet to understand how a scenario differs from its source sheet before applying it.
2146: get_shadow_sheet_row
2147: Toolset: scenario_planning
2148: get_shadow_sheet_row retrieves a single row from a scenario sheet by its row ID in a Scenario Planning scenario. The tool returns the full row data including cell values.
2149: Best Practices
2150: The following items are best practices for using the get_shadow_sheet_row tool:
2151: Call the get_shadow_sheet tool first to list rows and obtain valid row IDs before retrieving a specific row.
2152: Use this tool to confirm current cell values before performing an update with the update_shadow_sheet_rows tool.
2153: Basic Parameters
2154: The get_shadow_sheet_row tool has the following parameters:

2158: The get_shadow_sheet_row tool has the following key features:
2159: Single-row retrieval — Returns complete data for one row, including all cell values, without fetching the full scenario sheet.

2163: Only one row is returned per call.

2165: Requires at least Editor permissions on the workspace and all associated project sheets.
2166: Use Cases
2167: The following items describe use cases for the get_shadow_sheet_row tool:
2168: Pre-update verification — Confirm a row's current cell values before modifying it with the update_shadow_sheet_rows tool.
2169: Targeted data inspection — Retrieve a single row's data without loading the full scenario sheet, reducing response size.
2170: add_shadow_sheet_rows
2171: Toolset: scenario_planning
2172: add_shadow_sheet_rows adds one or more rows to a scenario sheet in a Scenario Planning scenario. Each row can specify where it is inserted using location specifiers. The tool returns the newly created rows.
2173: Best Practices
2174: The following items are best practices for using the add_shadow_sheet_rows tool:
2175: Call the get_shadow_sheet tool first to confirm the sheet structure and obtain column IDs.
2176: Ensure every row in the rows array specifies the same positioning attribute or an acceptable combination (toBottom, toTop, parentId, siblingId, or above). Split rows with different locations into separate calls.
2177: Use parentId to insert a row as a child of an existing row. Combine with toBottom=true to place it as the last child.
2178: Basic Parameters
2179: The add_shadow_sheet_rows tool has the following parameters:
2180: sheet_id — The ID of the scenario sheet to add rows to. This parameter is required. Obtain it from the source_sheet_ids field of a scenario returned by the get_scenario_groups tool with include_scenarios=true.
2181: rows — A list of one or more row objects to add. This parameter is required. Each row object can contain the following fields:
2182: cells — An optional array of cell objects. Each cell requires a columnId and either a value or a formula.
2183: toBottom, toTop — Booleans to position the row at the bottom or top of the sheet.
2184: parentId — The row ID of the parent row to nest this row under as a child.
2185: siblingId — The row ID to place this row next to at the same indentation level.
2186: above — When true, positions the row above the specified siblingId.
2187: indent, outdent — Number of levels to adjust the row's hierarchy. Must be used alone, without other location specifiers.
2188: expanded, locked, format — Optional row properties.
2189: Key Features
2190: The add_shadow_sheet_rows tool has the following key features:
2191: Flexible positioning — Supports toTop, toBottom, parentId, siblingId, and above location specifiers to insert rows at any position in the scenario sheet.
2192: Hierarchical placement — Use parentId and indent to create parent-child row relationships and multi-level hierarchies within the scenario.
2193: Batch insertion — Adds up to 500 rows in a single call for efficient scenario population.
2194: Limitations
2195: The add_shadow_sheet_rows tool has the following limitations:
2196: Maximum 500 rows per call.
2197: Does not support rows with image cells.
2198: The sheet_id must identify a scenario sheet, not a regular sheet.
2199: Every row in the rows array must specify the same positioning attribute or a compatible combination; rows with different locations require separate calls.
2200: Use Cases
2201: The following items describe use cases for the add_shadow_sheet_rows tool:
2202: Scenario population — Add new task rows to a scenario sheet to model additional work items in a "what-if" scenario before comparing it to the baseline.
2203: Hierarchical structure — Insert child rows under existing parent rows to add phases or subtasks within a scenario's project plan.
2204: Bulk row insertion — Add up to 500 rows in a single call to efficiently build out a scenario's scenario sheet.
2205: update_shadow_sheet_rows
2206: Toolset: scenario_planning
2207: The update_shadow_sheet_rows tool modifies one or more existing rows in a scenario sheet in a Scenario Planning scenario. Each row object must include a row ID identifying which row to update. The tool returns the updated rows.
2208: (⚠️ destructive, irreversible)
2209: Best Practices
2210: The following items are best practices for using the update_shadow_sheet_rows tool:
2211: Call the get_shadow_sheet tool first to retrieve row IDs, then call the get_shadow_sheet_row tool to confirm current cell values before updating.
2212: Include only the fields you want to change. Unspecified fields are left unchanged.
2213: Review the results for errors before calling the apply_scenario tool.
2214: Basic Parameters
2215: The update_shadow_sheet_rows tool has the following parameters:
2216: sheet_id — The ID of the scenario sheet containing the rows to update. This parameter is required. Obtain it from the source_sheet_ids field of a scenario returned by the get_scenario_groups tool with include_scenarios=true.
2217: rows — A list of one or more row objects to update. This parameter is required. Each row object must include the following fields:
2218: id — The ID of the row to update. This field is required.
2219: cells — An optional array of cell objects. Each cell requires a columnId and either a value or a formula.
2220: toBottom, toTop, parentId, siblingId, above, indent, outdent — Optional location specifiers to move the row simultaneously with updating its data.
2221: expanded, locked, format — Optional row properties.
2222: Key Features
2223: The update_shadow_sheet_rows tool has the following key features:
2224: Partial updates — Only modifies the fields you specify; all other row data remains unchanged.
2225: Combined data and position update — Updates cell values and repositions a row in a single operation using location specifiers.
2226: Batch updates — Modifies up to 500 rows in a single call.
2227: Limitations
2228: The update_shadow_sheet_rows tool has the following limitations:
2229: Maximum 500 rows per call.
2230: Updates are permanent within the scenario and cannot be automatically undone.
2231: The sheet_id must identify a scenario sheet, not a regular sheet.
2232: Each row object must include an id field; rows cannot be identified by position or content.
2233: Use Cases
2234: The following items describe use cases for the update_shadow_sheet_rows tool:
2235: Scenario adjustment — Modify task dates, assignments, or statuses in a scenario sheet to model a different resource allocation or timeline before comparing it to the baseline.
2236: Bulk cell updates — Change values across multiple rows in a single call to efficiently update a scenario's project data.
2237: Row repositioning — Move rows to different positions or hierarchy levels within the scenario sheet while simultaneously updating their cell values.
2238: delete_shadow_sheet_rows
2239: Toolset: scenario_planning
2240: The delete_shadow_sheet_rows tool permanently removes one or more rows from a scenario sheet in a Scenario Planning scenario by row ID. The response contains the IDs of all deleted rows, including child rows of any specified parent rows.
2241: (⚠️ destructive, irreversible)
2242: Best Practices
2243: The following items are best practices for using the delete_shadow_sheet_rows tool:
2244: Call the get_shadow_sheet tool first to retrieve rows and confirm their IDs before deleting.
2245: Verify the row hierarchy before deleting parent rows, as deleting a parent row also deletes all its child rows.

2247: The delete_shadow_sheet_rows tool has the following parameters:
